title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 23 (Public offer and private placement)

content.overview: Section 23 sets the permitted routes for issue of securities. A public company may issue securities (a) to the public through prospectus (public offer) by complying with Part I of Chapter III; or (b) through private placement by complying with Part II; or (c) through a rights issue or a bonus issue in accordance with the Act and, where listed or intending to list, also with the SEBI Act and regulations. A private company may issue securities only by rights issue or bonus issue, or through private placement under Part II. The Explanation provides that public offer includes IPO, FPO, or an offer for sale of securities to the public by an existing shareholder through a prospectus. Sub-sections (3) and (4) address prescribed classes of public companies listing in permissible foreign jurisdictions and Central Government power to exempt such classes from specified provisions.
content.glance: Public company: public offer / private placement / rights / bonus (SEBI if listed). Private company: rights / bonus / private placement only. Public offer includes IPO, FPO and OFS through prospectus.
content.study:
Section 23 is the gateway provision for Chapter III.

Statutory test
1. Public company routes under section 23(1): public offer through prospectus (Part I); private placement (Part II); rights or bonus issue (and SEBI law if listed or intending to list).
2. Private company routes under section 23(2): rights or bonus issue; private placement (Part II) only — no public offer.
3. Meaning of public offer (Explanation): IPO or FPO by the company, or offer for sale to the public by an existing shareholder, through issue of a prospectus.
4. Overseas listing (sub-sections (3)–(4)): prescribed class of public companies may issue prescribed class of securities for listing on permitted stock exchanges in permissible foreign jurisdictions; Central Government may by notification exempt such classes from specified provisions of Chapters III/IV and certain sections, with laying before Parliament.

Boundary
Section 23 identifies the route; the detailed rules for public offers sit in sections 24–41, and private placement in section 42. Listed or intending-to-list issues attract SEBI overlay in addition to the Companies Act.

sections.heading: Public company routes
sections.body: A public company may issue securities (a) to public through prospectus (public offer) by complying with Part I; or (b) through private placement by complying with Part II; or (c) through a rights issue or a bonus issue in accordance with the Act and, for listed companies or companies intending to list, also with the SEBI Act and regulations.

sections.heading: Private company routes
sections.body: A private company may issue securities only (a) by way of rights issue or bonus issue in accordance with the Act; or (b) through private placement by complying with Part II. It cannot make a public offer.

sections.heading: Meaning of public offer
sections.body: For the purposes of Chapter III, public offer includes initial public offer or further public offer of securities to the public by a company, or an offer for sale of securities to the public by an existing shareholder, through issue of a prospectus.

sections.heading: Overseas listing and exemption
sections.body: Such class of public companies as may be prescribed may issue such class of securities for listing on permitted stock exchanges in permissible foreign jurisdictions. The Central Government may by notification exempt any such class from specified provisions of Chapter III, Chapter IV, section 89, section 90 or section 127, with laying before both Houses of Parliament.

examples.title: Public company IPO
examples.body: A public company issues shares to the public through a prospectus. The route is a public offer under section 23(1)(a).

examples.title: Private company public offer (invalid)
examples.body: A private company attempts to offer shares to the public. Section 23(2) does not permit that route.

examples.title: Rights issue by private company
examples.body: A private company issues further shares pro rata to existing equity holders. The route is a rights issue under section 23(2)(a).

hypotheticals.question: Can a private company make an IPO?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 23(2) confines private companies to rights issue, bonus issue and private placement. Public offer is available only to public companies under section 23(1)(a).

distinctions.title: Public vs private company issue routes

rows.left: Public offer / private placement / rights / bonus

misconceptions.trap: Any company may freely make a public offer.
misconceptions.correction: Only a public company may make a public offer under section 23(1)(a).

misconceptions.trap: Section 23 itself contains all operational conditions for private placement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 23 identifies the route; private placement conditions sit in section 42 and the rules.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 23 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify company type (public or private). II. Classify the proposed issue. III. Apply the permitted route under section 23(1) or (2) and any SEBI overlay. IV. Conclude.
